acceptance: Under the product's settings (images https-only, video deny) Markdown assets refuse file, executable, blob and private-protocol URLs, credentials, plain http, SVG and oversized data images and workspace escapes, accept small raster data, credential-free https images and paths beside the document; workspace files are verified inside the root (no symlink escape, size limits); images and videos stay distinct kinds and video never loads remotely or from data.

reason: A hosted Markdown document resolves relative and root-relative assets inside its project through the provider, but an authored absolute `puppyone-cloud://` URL that points inside the same project root is refused natively (the product accepts it and rejects only other roots and token queries).

TS resolves Markdown assets through an AssetBroker that hands features capability URLs (including provider-resolved loopback URLs) under host leases it revokes, validates sinks and purposes, and runs trusted local HTML in revocable execution sessions. The native editor reads asset bytes itself through the workspace or provider after the same policy (no URLs, leases or capability purposes), and never executes HTML in Markdown (executable HTML is removed from the native flow).

acceptance: Only a lone credential-free https iframe becomes a web embed; localhost (also with a trailing dot or in capitals), local suffixes, private, loopback and IPv4-mapped addresses never load; one private DNS answer fails the whole resolution and the embed is pinned to the public addresses; at most a bounded number of embeds stay loaded per window, the least recently used invisible one evicted.

reason: Natively only the embed's top page is preflighted (one DNS resolution, every address public, pinned HTTPS) and its frames are limited to allowed origins. Its subresources are not filtered by scheme or DNS, a link the user activates to another origin is refused instead of opening in the browser (popups do open there), and downloads are not checked.

TS hosts web embeds as Electron WebContentsViews owned by a renderer: it checks the live owner and the IPC sender's main frame, clips and hides views by reported bounds, keeps the page while product chrome occludes it, reserves capacity while loading and destroys every view when its owner closes, crashes or fails to load. Native embeds are child web views inside the editor's own GPUI layout, released with their pane and window (bounded per-window pool).

Fragment links resolve only to headings natively. Controlled inline HTML ids (`<a id>`, `<span id>`) are not fragment targets, so explicit ids, their case-preserving lookup and precedence over heading slugs, their incremental rescans and the empty anchor as one deletion unit do not exist.
